original.description: A French Lebel mle 1886 rifle photographed side-on against a plain ground from the collection of the Armémuseum, Stockholm. The record describes the object as "Francoska repetirka Lebel M1886" — a Lebel M1886 repeating rifle — and does not say whether this example carries the 1893 modification.
original.photographer: Armémuseum (The Swedish Army Museum), Stockholm — the record credits the museum rather than an individual
original.date: catalogued image, uploaded 2015; the object is a Lebel mle 1886 (adopted 1886)
original.archive: Armémuseum (Swedish Army Museum), Stockholm; object record on DigitaltMuseum, 011024389339; via Wikimedia Commons
original.licence: CC BY-SA 3.0 (Commons record: LicenseShortName "CC BY-SA 3.0"; UsageTerms "Creative Commons Attribution-Share Alike 3.0"; AttributionRequired true). Share-alike: a derivative of this photograph would itself be CC BY-SA 3.0.

colorization.status: not colorized, and must not be — a modern colour photograph of the object, and share-alike would follow a derivative in any case.

content_policy: ok — a museum object photographed on its own; no casualties
caption: The Lebel mle 1886: the first smokeless-powder military rifle in the world, and by 1914 the oldest magazine system in the field — eight rounds in a tube under the barrel, fed one at a time. Armémuseum, Stockholm.
credit: Photograph: Armémuseum (The Swedish Army Museum), Stockholm, object 011024389339 on DigitaltMuseum, via Wikimedia Commons; CC BY-SA 3.0.
notes: Verified 2026-08-24 against the Commons file record via the MediaWiki API. The museum record does not distinguish the mle 1886 from the mle 1886 M93, so the caption and the card say mle 1886 and no more.
